assistant: "Let me validate the changes."
<commentary>
Manifest modified, validate to ensure correctness.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the manifest."
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- plugin-dev:skill-reviewer: Use this agent when the user has created or modified a skill and needs quality review, asks to "review my skill", "check skill quality", "improve skill description", or wants to ensure skill follows best practices. Trigger proactively after skill creation. Examples:

<example>
Context: User just created a new skill
user: "I've created a PDF processing skill"
assistant: "Great! Let me review the skill quality."
<commentary>
Skill created, proactively trigger skill-reviewer to ensure it follows best practices.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the skill."
</example>

<example>
Context: User requests skill review
user: "Review my skill and tell me how to improve it"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to analyze the skill quality."
<commentary>
Explicit skill review request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified skill description
user: "I updated the skill description, does it look good?"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the changes."
<commentary>
Skill description modified, review for triggering effectiveness.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. All three sub-agents have reported, and I've independently confirmed the working tree is untouched (diff stat identical to pre-dispatch, isolated test file still 8/8 green). Here is the consolidated report.

## Scale line

3 of 10 standing angles run, re-pointed at this step's actual risk surface; 6 dropped as vacuous and 1 folded in. **Dropped:** tokens/semantic-intent, styling conformance, structure (exports/stories), accessibility, story-interactivity-fidelity, and real-rendered-layout — all zero-touched here, since this diff changes no CSS, no JSX shape, no tokens, and no story (matches the plan's own explicit call that no live/visual verification is possible, Einstein being undeployed everywhere). **Folded in, not run separately:** "React logic correctness" — no new state was introduced, so this collapsed into Angle 1's mutation-testing of the one effect edit (the removed early-return) rather than standing alone. **Run:** (1) branch-render-logic falsification via real mutation testing, (2) recommender-gating specificity + sibling-regression + leftover-reference grep + See-Full-History link, (3) `tsc`/`npm run test` gate + imports/circular/later-sprint + magic-string/DRY. This is the first test pass on this uncommitted diff — nothing here is a re-run.

One correction mid-pass: my first `Read` of the test file returned stale/cached content that matched the file's *pre-diff* state almost verbatim, contradicting `git diff`. I didn't take it at face value — re-pulled the file via raw `bash cat -n` and confirmed the working tree genuinely holds the new (E1) content. Flagging this because it's a real tool-reliability gotcha worth knowing about, not just a footnote: a `Read` result disagreeing with `git diff` is a signal to re-verify via a second channel, not to trust the more convenient one.

One sub-agent dispatch was blocked by the permissions classifier: my first draft told it to `git checkout --` the file between mutations to "revert" — but since the whole file is *itself* uncommitted (the implementer's real work, no commit to fall back to), that command would have destroyed the entire Einstein implementation, not just the one-line test mutation. The classifier caught a real mistake in my own prompt. Relaunched with a `cp`-based scratchpad backup/restore instead (no git operations on the dirty file) — confirmed clean at the end (see Angle 1).

## Angle 1 — RV branch render-logic falsification (mutation-tested)

All 5 required scenarios exist as named test cases and the baseline suite is green (8/8):
`recommender=PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED with recs renders...` / `test.each` rows for `recs is an empty array (AC 8...)`, `recommendations has not resolved yet...`, `recs is undefined...` / `on the Cart route, renders null even when recs has items...`.

- **Empty-state gate is real, not decorative.** Mutating `if (!recommendations?.recs?.length)` → `if (false)` in `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx` made 3 of 8 tests go red for real (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')` on the undefined/not-yet-resolved cases, a wrong-element assertion on the empty-array case). **CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF.** Not a defect — this is the gate working.
- **Fetch-effect removal is real and tested for both RV and a sibling.** Commenting out `getRecommendations(recommender, _products)` failed 3/8 tests, including the non-RV `PDP_MIGHT_ALSO_LIKE` case. **CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF.** Not a defect.
- 🔵 **Note, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF:** reordering the Cart-check to run *after* the empty-recs check was **not** caught by any test — suite stayed green. This means the two guards' relative order is asserted in the module docblock ("no longer strictly matters either way... there's just no reason to move it") but not actually pinned by a test. Harmless today because both branches return unconditionally with no side effect before the `return` — but nothing would catch a future edit that adds one.
- **Dead-check unreachable for RV — confirmed structurally**, not just asserted: every one of the 3 possible execution paths through the RV `if` block (short-circuit at Cart, short-circuit at empty-recs, or fall through to the map/filter/map + return) ends in a `return` before reaching the base dead-check at `index.tsx:393`. **CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF** (this specific unreachability is RV-specific; the dead-check remains live and necessary for the other recommenders).
- 🔵 **Note, PLAUSIBLE, UNIFORM:** if a fetch **succeeds once** (populating real recs) and a **later re-fetch on the same mounted instance fails**, `useEinstein()`'s own catch block never calls `setRecommendations` (confirmed against `use-einstein.js:593-600`) — so the component would keep silently showing the **stale** prior recs with no error signal. This is not introduced by this diff and not fixable inside this file — every one of the 5 recommenders sharing this hook has the identical blind spot via the same pattern (the base dead-check has the same "no signal on a failed re-fetch" hole). Named here because it's real, not because this step owns it.

Restore proof, independently re-checked by me after the sub-agent finished: `git diff --stat` still shows exactly the original 166 insertions/287 deletions across the same two files, and `npx vitest run` on the isolated file still reports 8/8 passing.

## Angle 2 — Recommender-gating specificity, sibling regression, leftover references, See-Full-History

- **No collision.** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants.js:155-160`: `ADD_TO_CART_MODAL`/`PDP_MIGHT_ALSO_LIKE` = `'pdp-similar-items'`, `CART_MAY_ALSO_LIKE` = `'product-to-product-einstein'`, `PDP_COMPLETE_SET` = `'complete-the-set'`, `CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`/`PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` = `'viewed-recently-einstein'`. None of the four non-RV recommenders collides with the RV string. **CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF.** 🔵 Side note: `ADD_TO_CART_MODAL` and `PDP_MIGHT_ALSO_LIKE` are themselves identical strings — pre-existing vendor duplication, not this diff's concern, not actionable from `overrides/`.
- **Sibling code path is byte-identical, not just untested-into-breaking.** Diff-hunk boundaries confirm zero changes below the RV `if` block's closing brace (new-file lines 383-497) — the strongest possible evidence the 4 siblings didn't regress, independent of test coverage.
- 🔵 **Note, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM:** only **one** non-RV value (`PDP_MIGHT_ALSO_LIKE`) is actually exercised anywhere in `index.test.tsx`; `ADD_TO_CART_MODAL`, `CART_MAY_ALSO_LIKE`, `PDP_COMPLETE_SET` never appear. The reasoning that this is sufficient (a pure `===` check has exactly two outcomes, and the untested three can't reach any path the tested one doesn't) is sound and I find it convincing *today*. But it's a structural argument standing in for direct verification, and it's the same single-stand-in pattern this file's suite has always used — worth a cheap `test.each` over the other three names as insurance if this file is touched again, not a blocker now.
- **Leftover references: zero hits**, exactly matching the plan's own pass criterion:
  `grep -n "useRecentlyViewedHistory\|useRecentlyViewedProductFetch\|hasRecentlyViewed\|recentlyViewedIds\|NO_RECENTLY_VIEWED_IDS" overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.test.tsx` → no output. **CONFIRMED.**
- 🔵 One `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` hit at `index.tsx:365`, inside a comment — this is the plan's own already-named, already-deferred-to-a-later-cleanup-step item, not a new defect from this diff.
- **See-Full-History link: real, non-trivial boundary test.** `seeAllHref` is only ever `buildUrl(RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE)`, gated by `showSeeAllLink`; the two tests sit exactly at the threshold (2 cards vs. `base` visible-count of 2 → link absent; 3 cards → link present) and assert genuinely opposite outcomes (`toBe('/en-GB/recently-viewed')` vs. `toBeUndefined()`), not two assertions that would both pass regardless of correctness. **CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF.**

## Angle 3 — Compiles/passes, imports, magic-string/DRY

- **`npx tsc --noEmit`** → exit code 0, no output. **CONFIRMED CLEAN.**
- **`npm run test` (full suite)**, real numbers: `Test Files 87 passed (87)`, `Tests 1324 passed (1324)`, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 14.93s. Isolated file: `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 8 passed (8)`. **CONFIRMED CLEAN.** (Benign pre-existing stderr noise — CSS-parse/missing-translation warnings — appears across many unrelated files too, not introduced here.)
- **Imports**: `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` and `selectRecentlyViewedCard`/`RecentlyViewedCard`/`RecentlyViewedProduct` both correctly relative (`../ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail`, `../../utils/recentlyViewedCard`); zero remaining imports of the two now-orphaned interim modules in these two files; no `../../../../`+ chains; no circular import (`recommended-products` string absent from all four of its own non-vendor imports); nothing from an unfamiliar/later-sprint path. **CONFIRMED CLEAN**, all six sub-checks.
- **Magic-string check**: one hit for the literal `'viewed-recently-einstein'`, and it's inside the module docblock's own explanatory comment (`index.tsx:41`), not executable code — exactly the documented-precedent case the plan allows. **CONFIRMED CLEAN.**

## What I tried to falsify

Defeated the empty-state gate directly (code went red as it should); removed the fetch call entirely (code went red for RV and a sibling); reordered the two guards to see if anything actually pins their sequence (nothing does — a real, if currently harmless, gap); hunted for a recommender-string collision across all 6 constants (none, other than the pre-accepted Cart/PDP identity); grepped for every interim-mechanism symbol across both changed files (zero); tried to find a trivially-satisfiable pair of See-Full-History tests (found a real threshold boundary instead); looked for a base-path import shadowing an override, a circular import, a too-deep relative chain (none); looked for a duplicated magic-string standing in for the constant (none in live code). Everything that could be run, was run — nothing here is a description taken on faith.

## What I could not verify

Everything here is bounded by the same hard ceiling the plan itself names: **Einstein is undeployed everywhere reachable**, so nothing above is verified against a real API response — only against mocked shapes and the vendor hook's source code. Specifically unverifiable: whether RV genuinely needs no seed products (plan's own Open Question 3); whether a real Business-Manager-configured recommender's response actually matches the merged shape `fetchRecProductDetails` produces in `use-einstein.js` (the *code* that does the merging is confirmed real, but its real-world output isn't observable pre-deployment); the stale-recs-on-failed-refetch scenario (Angle 1, reasoned from the hook's source, not exercised — the hook is fully mocked in this test file, and constructing that transition would mean adding new test code, which is the implementer's job, not mine). Out of my scope entirely: E2/E3/E4 (page, PDP write-path, deletions) were not touched by this diff and weren't tested here; the plan's separate "Final gate" (local CodeRabbit review) hasn't run yet and isn't part of this step's pass criteria.

## What Marcel is missing

The stale-recs-on-a-failed-re-fetch gap (Angle 1, item 5) isn't owned by this PR and isn't fixable inside this file — but it's real, silent, and shared by all five/six recommenders through the same base hook and the same "dead-check never distinguishes never-fetched from just-failed" pattern. Worth a ticket of its own rather than staying implicit, since it'll otherwise only ever surface as a confusing bug report ("the rail shows the wrong products") with no error anywhere to point at.
